{{Location map|Japan Shimane Prefecture| label = Tsukuriyama Kofun Group| position = top| mark = Red pog.svg| marksize = 10| relief = 1| width = 250| caption={{left|Location.}}}}

'''Tsukuriyama Kofun Group''' (造山古墳群, Tsukuriyama Kofungun) is a {{ill|Kofun cluster|ja|古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun group|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun cluster}} from the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}} located in {{ill|Yasugi, Shimane|ar|ياسوغي (شيمانه)|azb|یاسوقی، شیمانه|bg|Ясуги|ca|Yasugi|ce|Ясуги|ceb|Yasugichō|de|Yasugi|es|Yasugi (Shimane)|fa|یاسوگی، شیمانه|fi|Yasugi|fr|Yasugi|gl|Yasugi|id|Yasugi, Shimane|it|Yasugi|ja|安来市|ko|야스기시|mg|Yasugichō|mzn|یاسوگی، شیمانه|nl|Yasugi|pl|Yasugi|pt|Yasugi|ro|Yasugi|ru|Ясуги|sv|Yasugi|tg|Ясуги|tl|Yasugi, Shimane|tr|Yasugi|tt|Ясуги|uk|Ясуґі|ur|یاسگی، شیمانے|vi|Yasugi, Shimane|war|Yasugi, Shimane|zh|安來市|zh_classical|安來市|zh_min_nan|Yasugi-chhī|zh_yue|安來|qid=Q851114|lt=Yasugi, Shimane}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|qid=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture}}. Together with other nearby Kofun groups, it has been collectively designated as the "'''Arashima Kofun Group''' (荒島古墳群)" and recognized as a {{ill|Historic site|en|Historic site|qid=Q1081138|lt=Historic site of Japan}}} by the Japanese government.<ref name=shimanebunkazai>{{Cite web|author=Shimane Prefecture Education and Cultural Properties Division|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shiseki/kunisiseki.html|title=List of National Cultural Properties [Historic Sites]|work=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2023-08-27}}</ref><ref name=bunkaisan>{{Cite web|author=Agency for Cultural Affairs|url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/heritages/detail/172875|title=Arashima Kofun Group|work=Cultural Heritage Online|accessdate=2023-08-27}}</ref>{{Refnest|group=Note|Tsukuriyama is categorized as a '''subgroup of the Arashima Kofun Group'''.<ref name=bunkaisan/>}} It is also part of the broader {{ill|Arashima Kofun Cluster|ja|荒島墳墓群|qid=Q121863310}}. The Yasugi City government has developed the area into a historical park named "'''Ancient Izumo Royal Mausoleum Hill'''" (古代出雲王陵の丘).<ref name=shimaneOuryounooka>{{Cite web|author=Shimane Prefecture Education and Cultural Properties Division|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shiseki/shisekidesu/shiseki01.html|title=Shimane Historic Sites: Ancient Izumo Royal Mausoleum Hill|work=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2023-08-27}}</ref><ref name=yasukiOuryounooka>{{Cite web|author=Yasugi City Tourism Association|url=https://yasugi-kankou.com/spot/spot-482/|title=Ancient Izumo Royal Mausoleum Hill|work=Yasugi City Tourism Guide|accessdate=2023-08-27}}</ref>.

== Overview ==

[[File:造山1号墳出土 円筒埴輪 (J-34492).JPG|thumb|160px|right|{{center|Cylindrical haniwa from Tsukuriyama 1 Kofun}}{{small|Exhibited at {{ill|Tokyo National Museum|en|Tokyo National Museum|qid=Q653433|lt=Tokyo National Museum}}.}}]]
'''Tsukuriyama 1 Kofun''' is a {{ill|Square Kofun|ja|方墳}} measuring 60 meters on each side, one of the largest square mounds from the early Kofun period nationwide. Excavations in {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=1936}} (Shōwa 11) and 1938 (Shōwa 13) revealed a {{ill|Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|zh|豎穴式石室|qid=Q11598499}}. Buried artifacts include {{ill|Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|ja|三角縁神獣鏡}}, {{ill|TLV mirror|es|Espejo TLV|fr|Miroir TLV|id|Cermin TLV|ja|方格規矩鏡|qid=Q3316102|lt=square-rim deity-and-animal mirrors}}, spindle-shaped stone artifacts, glass {{ill|Kudatama|ja|管玉|lt=Tubular beads}}, iron swords, and {{ill|Kozuka|ja|刀子|qid=Q11396050|lt=Ko-dachi}}. On December 16, 1936, it was designated a National Historic Site under the name "Tsukuriyama Kofun."{{Sfn|Nagami|Miyake|1992|p=1}}

'''Tsukuriyama 3 Kofun''' is a square mound dating to the early Kofun period, measuring 38 meters in length and 30 meters in width. Excavations in {{ill|1965|en|1965|qid=Q2650|lt=1965}} uncovered a pit-style stone chamber yielding a {{ill|two-deity two-beast mirror|ja|斜縁神獣鏡|qid=Q109594939}}, jasper tubular beads, glass beads, a ko-dachi, and a yari-ganna (drawknife). It was designated a Shimane Prefecture Historic Site on May 31, 1965.{{Sfn|Nagami|Miyake|1992|p=1}}

On the highest point of the hill, there is '''Tsukuriyama 2 Kofun''', a {{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|lt=Zenpō-kōhō-fun}} measuring 50 meters in length, and the smaller '''Tsukuriyama 4 Kofun'''. Both were excavated in 1991, revealing construction dating to the early 6th century.{{Sfn|Nagami|Miyake|1992}} A fifth mound, '''Tsukuriyama 5 Kofun''', is located slightly apart from the main group.

Nearby, the '''Ōnari Kofun''', another square mound from the early Kofun period, is the largest of its kind nationally. Excavations in {{ill|1911|en|1911|qid=Q2076|lt=1911}} revealed artifacts such as triangular-rimmed deity-and-beast mirrors and a {{ill|sokantō|ja|素環頭大刀}}. A reproduction of the sokantō, crafted by master swordsmith {{ill|Kunihira Kawachi|ja|河内国平|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawachi Kunihira|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 河内國平|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11553389}}, is exhibited at the {{ill|Wakō Museum|ja|和鋼博物館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yasugi City Wako Museum|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11418233}}.

== Cultural Properties ==
Initially, Tsukuriyama 1 Kofun was designated as a National Historic Site, and Tsukuriyama 3 Kofun was designated as a Shimane Prefecture Historic Site. In 1999, the Agency for Cultural Affairs expanded the designation to include Tsukuriyama Kofun Group (2-4 Kofun), Ōnari Kofun, and the Shiozuyama Burial Group (1-11 Kofun), officially renaming them the "'''Arashima Kofun Group'''".<ref name=shimanebunkazai/><ref name=bunkaisan/>
